<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XV.|OF THE APOSTLES.|335}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}}† Then it pleased the Apostles and Auncients vvith the vvhole Church, to chose men out of them, & to send to Antioche vvith Paul and Barnabas, Iudas, vvho vvas surnamed Barsabas, & Silas, cheefe men among the brethren, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Other latin copies and the greeke read thus, ''Writing by their handes an epistle conteining these things''.}}∷ vvriting by their handes.

The Apostles and Auncients, the brethren, to the brethren of the Gentiles that are at Antioche and in Syria and Cilicia, greeting. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}}† Because vve haue heard that certaine {{sup|‖}} going forth from vs, haue troubled you vvith vvordes, subuerting your soules, to vvhom vve gaue no commaundement: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}}† it hath pleased vs being gathered in one, to chose out men and to send them vnto you vvith our deerest Barnabas and Paul, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=26}}† men that haue giuen their liues for the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=27}}† We haue sent therfore Iudas & Silas, vvho them selues also wil in vvordes report vnto you the same things. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=28}}† For it hath seemed good {{sup|‖}} to the holy Ghost & to vs, to lay no further burden vpon you then these necessarie things: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=29}}† that you absteine from the things immolated to Idols, and bloud, and that vvhich is strangled, and {{sup|‖}} fornication, from the vvhich things keeping your selues, you shal doe vvell. Fare ye vvel.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=30}}† They therfore being dimissed went downe to Antioche: and gathering the multitude, deliuered the epistle. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=31}}† Vvhich vvhen they had read, they {{sup|‖}} reioyced vpon the consolation: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=32}}† but Iudas and Silas, them Selues also being prophets, vvith many vvordes comforted the brethren, and confirmed them. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=33}}† And hauing spent some time there, they vvere vvith peace dimissed of the brethren vnto them that had sent them. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=34}}† But it seemed good vnto Silas to remaine there: and Iudas departed alone: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=35}}† and Paul and Barnabas taried at Antioche, teaching and euangelizing vvith many others the vvord of our Lord.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=36}}† And after certaine daies, Paul said to Barnabas, Let vs returne and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 13, 14.''}}* visite our brethren in al cities vvherein vve {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Hereof our Catholike Bishops tooke vp the necessarie vse of often visiting their flockes & cures committed to their charge, for confirmation in faith & vertue, & reformation of maners both of clergie & laitie. · Act. 13, 14.}}∷ haue preached the vvord of our Lord, how they doe. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=37}}† And Barnabas vvould haue taken vvith them Iohn also that vvas surnamed Marke. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=38}}† But Paul desired that he (as vvho {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 13, 13.''}}* had departed from them out of Pamphylia, and had not gone vvith them to the vvorke) might not be receiued. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=39}}† And there rose a {{sup|‖}} dissention, so that they departed one from an other, & that Barnabas in deede taking Marke sailed to Cypres. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=40}}† But<noinclude>{{rh|||Paul}}</noinclude>
